program: Interdisciplinary Graduate Program (IGP) / Quantitative and Chemical Biology (QCB) pathways

requirements.quote: Successful applicants have extensive independent, hypothesis-driven laboratory research experience, strong grades in their STEM courses, and strong recommendation letters that speak to the applicant’s research experience and interest.

Successful applicants have extensive independent, hypothesis-driven laboratory research experience, strong grades in their STEM courses, and strong recommendation letters that speak to the applicant’s research experience and interest.
Students entering QCB typically have earned undergraduate degrees in chemistry, physics, computer science, engineering, or mathematics.

Applicants with a background and coursework in the quantitative sciences such as engineering, physics, chemistry, computer science or data science without many/any biology courses are a great fit for the QCB program.

problems: Neither IGP nor QCB admissions/FAQ/prospective-student pages name any required or recommended math, statistics or programming coursework; only holistic-review/typical-background statements (strong STEM grades; QCB suits applicants with math/physics/chemistry/CS/engineering backgrounds). not_stated=true for math coursework.
IGP is aimed at applicants with a strong biology background; QCB at quantitative backgrounds with limited biology.
